A Primer on Categories, Presheaves, and Simplicial Sets

Diogo Andrade

Categories and posets

A category C\mathcal CC consists of objects and, for each pair of objects x,yx,yx,y, a set Hom⁡C(x,y)\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(x,y)HomC​(x,y) of morphisms. Composition is associative and each object xxx has an identity idx\mathrm{id}_xidx​.

A partially ordered set, or poset, is a set PPP with a reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive relation ≤\leq≤. A poset is itself a category. Its objects are the elements of PPP, and there is one arrow x→yx\to yx→y if x≤yx\leq yx≤y. Reflexivity supplies the identities and transitivity supplies composition.

The simplex category Δ\DeltaΔ is the category of finite nonempty ordinals [n]={0<1<⋯<n}[n]=\{0<1<\cdots<n\}[n]={0<1<⋯<n} and weakly increasing maps. Two families of maps do much of the work:

  • The face map δi:[n−1]→[n]\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]δi​:[n−1]→[n] misses iii and is strictly increasing.
  • The degeneracy map σi:[n]→[n−1]\sigma_i:[n]\to[n-1]σi​:[n]→[n−1] repeats iii and is surjective.

For example, the face maps [0]→[1][0]\to[1][0]→[1] select the two endpoints. The degeneracy map [1]→[0][1]\to[0][1]→[0] sends both endpoints to the same point. Every map in Δ\DeltaΔ factors uniquely as a surjection onto its image followed by the inclusion of that image. In particular, each surjection is a composite of degeneracy maps.

Functors and natural transformations

A functor F:C→DF:\mathcal C\to\mathcal DF:C→D assigns objects and morphisms while preserving identities and composition. Functors between posets are order-preserving maps. Another example comes from a group GGG. Form the one-object category BGBGBG with GGG as its endomorphisms. A functor BG→SetBG\to\mathbf{Set}BG→Set is a left GGG-set.

A natural transformation η:F⇒G\eta:F\Rightarrow Gη:F⇒G gives a morphism ηc:F(c)→G(c)\eta_c:F(c)\to G(c)ηc​:F(c)→G(c) for every object ccc so that for each f:c→df:c\to df:c→d,

G(f)∘ηc=ηd∘F(f). G(f)\circ\eta_c=\eta_d\circ F(f). G(f)∘ηc​=ηd​∘F(f).
Both sides go from F(c)F(c)F(c) to G(d)G(d)G(d). This is the naturality square written as an equation.

Presheaves, limits, and colimits

A presheaf on C\mathcal CC is a functor X:Cop→SetX:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}X:Cop→Set. Each object ccc determines a representable presheaf Hom⁡C(−,c)\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)HomC​(−,c). Its restriction map along f:x→yf:x\to yf:x→y sends g:y→cg:y\to cg:y→c to g∘fg\circ fg∘f.

The Yoneda lemma says that evaluating a natural transformation at idc\mathrm{id}_cidc​ gives a bijection

Nat⁡(Hom⁡C(−,c),X)≅X(c). \operatorname{Nat}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,c),X)\cong X(c). Nat(HomC​(−,c),X)≅X(c).
To see the inverse, take a∈X(c)a\in X(c)a∈X(c). At an object ddd, send each g:d→cg:d\to cg:d→c to X(g)(a)X(g)(a)X(g)(a). Naturality forces precisely this formula. Taking XXX representable gives the fully faithful Yoneda embedding of C\mathcal CC into its presheaf category.

Let F:J→CF:J\to\mathcal CF:J→C be a diagram. A cone with apex ccc is a family λj:c→F(j)\lambda_j:c\to F(j)λj​:c→F(j) compatible with the arrows in JJJ. Its universal object, when it exists, represents the presheaf Cone⁡(−,F)\operatorname{Cone}(-,F)Cone(−,F):

Hom⁡C(c,lim⁡JF)≅Cone⁡(c,F). \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,\lim_J F)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(c,F). HomC​(c,Jlim​F)≅Cone(c,F).
Equivalently, a limit cone is a terminal object in the category of cones. The colimit is the dual construction, using cocones and an initial object.

The category of elements of a presheaf XXX has objects (c,a)(c,a)(c,a) with a∈X(c)a\in X(c)a∈X(c). An arrow (c,a)→(d,b)(c,a)\to(d,b)(c,a)→(d,b) is an arrow f:c→df:c\to df:c→d for which X(f)(b)=aX(f)(b)=aX(f)(b)=a. This construction lets us regard all the elements of a presheaf, at all objects of C\mathcal CC, in a single category.

Simplicial sets

A simplicial set is a presheaf XXX on Δ\DeltaΔ. Write Xn=X([n])X_n=X([n])Xn​=X([n]). Applying XXX to δi\delta_iδi​ gives a face operator di:Xn→Xn−1d_i:X_n\to X_{n-1}di​:Xn​→Xn−1​, and applying it to σi\sigma_iσi​ gives a degeneracy operator si:Xn−1→Xns_i:X_{n-1}\to X_nsi​:Xn−1​→Xn​.

A simplex x∈Xnx\in X_nx∈Xn​ is degenerate if x=X(α)(y)x=X(\alpha)(y)x=X(α)(y) for some surjection α:[n]→[m]\alpha:[n]\to[m]α:[n]→[m] with m<nm<nm<n and y∈Xmy\in X_my∈Xm​. Using the factorization of surjections in Δ\DeltaΔ, prove that this is equivalent to xxx being in the image of a single sis_isi​.

The standard simplex Δn\Delta^nΔn is the presheaf represented by [n][n][n], so that

(Δn)m=Hom⁡Δ([m],[n]). (\Delta^n)_m=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([m],[n]). (Δn)m​=HomΔ​([m],[n]).
Yoneda identifies a map Δn→X\Delta^n\to XΔn→X with an nnn-simplex of XXX. This gives a precise meaning to the idea of building XXX by gluing together standard simplices.

Exercises

  1. For a covariant functor F:C→SetF:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}F:C→Set, identify its category of elements with the comma category {∗}↓F\{\ast\}\downarrow F{∗}↓F.
  2. Find a terminal object of the slice category C/c\mathcal C_{/c}C/c​ and show that it is terminal.
  3. View Hom⁡C(−,−)\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,-)HomC​(−,−) as a functor Cop×C→Set\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}Cop×C→Set. Describe the objects and arrows of its category of elements. Why is it called the twisted arrow category?
  4. Prove that the projection from the category of elements of a presheaf to C\mathcal CC is a discrete right fibration. Formulate and prove the dual statement for a covariant functor.
  5. Show that limits and colimits of presheaves are computed objectwise.
  6. Show that XXX is the colimit of the diagram of representables Hom⁡C(−,c)\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)HomC​(−,c) indexed by its category of elements. At an object ddd, the maps into X(d)X(d)X(d) send (c,a,g:d→c)(c,a,g:d\to c)(c,a,g:d→c) to X(g)(a)X(g)(a)X(g)(a). Apply this to simplicial sets.
